items.title: Larry Gold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2025
items.q: He was also Pablo Casals' first call in the Bach orchestra suites at Marlboro.

ctx.x: Look him up. He was Leonard Bernstein's first call for like when he did his Broadway shows, you know, in that pit band he was Leonard Bernstein's first call. Brilliant violin — he was also Pablo Casals' first call in the Bach orchestra suites at Marlboro. He was a brilliant musician. I don't think he went to Curtis. When I was there there was a young man who played the clarinet named Weldon Berry who was from Philadelphia, who was a black clarinet player. And my best friend growing up was Renard Edwards who is a…
have to say for someone who is 80 years old he still looked brilliant and still plays and that viola is so heavy and I don't understand how he can still do it.
